result.title: Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments
result.summary: Tool-call judges evaluate argument values proposed by LLM agents. We find that they accept a correct value less often when their input holds no reference for it, that is, no text that says what the value should be. This happens when the value is a default value from the function schema that the user did not mention, when it has to be inferred, or when the text it comes from was cut from the judge input. We call this drop in acceptance the derivation gap. It appears across all seven judges we evaluate, including System One models CLM and Jev. The gap is not only a truncation artifact: correct default values have the largest gap on a benchmark with no truncation. A controlled source-relocation test shows that judges follow the reference in their input: they favor a visible incorrect value over a correct value whose source is hidden. We introduce DeRef (Derived Reference): a separate model reads the full history without seeing the candidate and writes a reference for the judge. Across three benchmarks, DeRef improves overall argument AUROC for all judges tested. On the controlled test, it raises AUROC from chance or below to between 98.40 and 99.59.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察工具调用评审模型（judge）对参数取值的判定：当输入中缺少说明该值应为何值的参考文本时，正确取值被接受的比例下降，作者称之为「derivation gap」，并在七个 judge 上复现；为此提出 DeRef，用一个单独模型在不看候选值的情况下读取完整历史、写出参考供 judge 使用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「判定高度依赖输入中可见参考、来源被隐藏即偏向错误值」的结论，可能为 VLM 推理答案核验、证据筛选与 latent 内容使用程度的诊断提供可借鉴的方法线索，但该工作本身限于文本工具调用场景，与视觉推理无直接关联。
